_comment: Registry of explanations for current mismatch buckets, keyed by (suite, concept, kind) and optionally disambiguated by `engines` when two reports share a suite slug. The dashboard renders the cause inline next to the disagreement count. Entries only render next to live mismatch buckets, so suites with zero mismatches need no entry; delete entries when their bucket clears.

entries.label: PE-imputed MA TAFDC income plus categorical/BBCE input gaps
entries.description: 65 of 896 MA households differ on benefit amount. Two causes: PolicyEngine imputes MA TAFDC/TANF into SNAP unearned income while Axiom projects only observed ECPS income facts, and PE pays households through a categorical/BBCE path whose TANF-service and authorization facts are not yet available to Axiom's projection. Utilities are not a driver: the FY 2026 heating/cooling SUA is encoded at $914/month and matches PE in every traced residual.

drivers.label: MA TAFDC/TANF missing from Axiom SNAP unearned income
drivers.description: In the Axiom-greater-than-PE residuals, PE computes MA TAFDC and counts it in SNAP unearned income; Axiom does not compute or inject it.
evidence: PE has positive MA TAFDC/TANF in 31 of the traced mismatching households.
ecps-3317: Axiom $785 vs PE $450.32; PE unearned income includes $11,127.63/year of MA TAFDC.
ecps-3328: Axiom $307 vs PE $23.97; PE MA TAFDC is $9,536/year.

drivers.label: Categorical/BBCE path encoded but input-limited
drivers.description: Residuals paired with Axiom-ineligible/$0 vs PE-eligible-positive trace to Axiom categorical outputs being false because TANF-service, EAEDC/TAFDC authorization, and categorical income-standard facts are missing from the ECPS projection. The 106 CMR 365.180(A) rollup is wired (`snap_income_eligible = categorical OR standard`); the gap is inputs, not compose.
evidence: ecps-3419 and ecps-3716 pass Axiom core, residency, and resource gates but fail standard income with categorical outputs false.
Eligibility mismatches split 39 PE-only / 3 Axiom-only.

entries.label: MA categorical/BBCE facts incomplete
entries.description: 39 households are PE-eligible but Axiom-ineligible. The 106 CMR 365.180(A) categorical rollup is encoded and composed, but the traced cases still resolve categorical outputs to false because TANF-service, EAEDC/TAFDC authorization, and gross categorical income-standard facts are missing or source-unresolved in the ECPS projection.

entries.label: MA gross-cap treatment divergence
entries.description: 3 households are Axiom-eligible but PE-ineligible. The inspected case is a disabled one-person household at about 210.6% FPG gross / 95.2% FPG net: Axiom passes the federal elderly/disabled net-income path while PE rejects under its MA gross/categorical treatment.

entries.label: PE-imputed AL TANF income plus small edges
entries.description: 24 of 704 AL households differ on benefit amount. 21 are PE-imputed Alabama TANF counted in SNAP unearned income that Axiom does not project; the rest are one threshold/disqualification edge, one environment-sensitive minimum-benefit case, and one $7.78 residual just over the $7 tolerance.

drivers.label: Alabama TANF missing from Axiom SNAP unearned income
drivers.description: 21 of the 22 Axiom-greater-than-PE residuals have positive PE-imputed `al_tanf` in SNAP unearned income.
evidence: ecps-51206: Axiom $785 vs PE $749.27; PE al_tanf = $4,128/year.
ecps-51308: Axiom $546 vs PE $520.93; PE al_tanf = $3,648/year.

drivers.label: Non-TANF edges
drivers.description: ecps-51708 is an Axiom-eligible/PE-ineligible disqualification edge with no TANF and PE net income near 41% FPG. ecps-51400 is PE-eligible at $23.97/month under the pinned dashboard runner but $0 in the local environment, so it is an oracle-environment discrepancy rather than an Axiom formula bug. ecps-51859 is a $7.78 amount residual.
evidence: Pinned runner: policyengine==4.11.0, policyengine-us==1.700.0, policyengine-core==3.26.11.
ecps-51859: Axiom $828 vs PE $835.78.

entries.label: Zero-weight TANF and disqualification edges
entries.description: 3 households are Axiom-eligible but PE-ineligible, all with household weight 0. Two are TANF interactions where PE-imputed AL TANF pushes net income just over 100% FPG (ecps-51544 at 106.1%, ecps-52446 at 103.5%); ecps-51708 has no TANF and PE net income near 41% FPG, a PE disqualification or categorical-source edge.

entries.label: Minimum-benefit eligibility edge, environment-sensitive
entries.description: 1 household is PE-eligible with a positive minimum benefit while Axiom fails the standard net-income gate. The same case returns PE-ineligible/$0 in the local environment, so this is an income/categorical eligibility edge plus a PE-environment reproducibility issue, not a broken minimum-benefit formula.

entries.label: PE-imputed TN Families First income
entries.description: 31 of 852 TN households differ on benefit amount. 30 are Axiom-greater-than-PE with positive PE-imputed Families First/TANF in SNAP unearned income that Axiom does not project. The single PE-greater case (ecps-50388) has no TANF and is an untraced amount edge. The encoded TN utility allowance table is not the driver: PE applies zero SNAP utility allowance in every mismatch case.

drivers.label: Families First missing from Axiom SNAP unearned income
drivers.description: PE includes `tn_ff` in SNAP unearned income; Axiom's ECPS projection has no Families First fact.
evidence: ecps-49363: Axiom $909 vs PE $733.70; PE tn_ff = $5,652/year.
ecps-49502: Axiom $563 vs PE $429.28; PE tn_ff = $5,652/year.
ecps-50388 (PE-greater): tn_ff and tanf are $0, PE net income about 53.3% FPG.

drivers.label: TN utility table encoded but not safely composable
drivers.description: The SUA/BUA/telephone amounts sit in `regulations/1240-01/04/27/block-1` together with stale SNAP income standards and allotment values, so the block cannot be composed wholesale without overriding current federal FY 2026 values. Real wiring gap, but not the observed residual driver.
evidence: PE `snap_utility_allowance > 0` in 0 of the TN benefit-mismatch cases.

entries.label: Families First income pushes PE over the net-income edge
entries.description: 5 households are Axiom-eligible but PE-ineligible, all with positive PE-imputed Families First and PE net income between 103.6% and 108.2% FPG. Axiom passes standard income because it does not project Families First into SNAP unearned income. Only ecps-49447 is weighted.

entries.label: PE-imputed SC TANF income plus minimum-benefit categorical cases
entries.description: 61 of 758 SC households differ on benefit amount. The large weighted residuals are PE-imputed `sc_tanf` counted in SNAP unearned income that Axiom does not project. Most of the rest are minimum-benefit cases where PE is eligible at about $23.97/month while Axiom fails the standard net-income and categorical gates. Shelter/utility math is not the driver: traced cases show PE utility allowance and excess-shelter deduction both zero.

drivers.label: SC TANF missing from Axiom SNAP unearned income
drivers.description: Traced high-dollar residuals all show PE adding sc_tanf on top of observed income while Axiom uses only observed ECPS facts.
evidence: ecps-40496: PE gross income includes sc_tanf = $4,303.43/year.
ecps-40667: PE adds sc_tanf = $5,425.18/year on top of observed SSI.
Traced cases ecps-40496/40667/41488/41512/41554/41761/41881 all have PE snap_utility_allowance = 0.

drivers.label: Minimum-benefit cases blocked by SC categorical gates
drivers.description: Weighted traced cases pass Axiom core, residency, resource, and gross-income gates but fail net income and the composed categorical income gate, while PE pays the federal minimum.
evidence: ecps-40398, ecps-40588, ecps-40900, ecps-41287, ecps-41409, ecps-41604, ecps-41647: Axiom standard-net false and categorical false; PE about $23.97/month.

entries.label: PE broader categorical path vs SC source
entries.description: 29 households are PE-eligible but Axiom-ineligible. The SC source ties expanded categorical eligibility to Family Independence Information and Referral Services with income at or below 130% FPL; PE appears to allow these cases through a broader gross-FPG categorical path (traced PE gross FPG ratios run 1.13 to 1.95). Wiring the broader path into Axiom would be synthetic unless encoder/source review establishes it.

entries.label: Zero-weight SC TANF income interaction
entries.description: 6 households are Axiom-eligible but PE-ineligible, all with household weight 0. PE adds imputed SC TANF to SNAP unearned income and denies (e.g. ecps-40402 at 104.2% FPG net, ecps-40659 at 116.0% FPG net); Axiom uses only observed ECPS income facts and passes.

entries.label: Mostly small residuals; large ones are TANF-on-SSI
entries.description: 40 of 1,366 NC households differ on benefit amount. 31 are within $12 and 34 within $25. Only 2 exceed $100, and both are the cross-state TANF pattern: PE adds imputed `nc_tanf` to SNAP unearned income on top of observed SSI, while Axiom has no TANF fact to project. The earlier large non-TANF residuals were eliminated by projecting the case shelter fact into PE `housing_cost` (79 residuals before the projection fix, 40 after).

drivers.label: TANF-on-SSI residuals
drivers.description: Both over-$100 residuals pair PE-imputed NC TANF with observed SSI.
evidence: ecps-39544: PE unearned income is SSI $11,928/year plus nc_tanf = $3,264/year.
ecps-40017: PE unearned income is SSI $11,928/year plus nc_tanf = $2,832/year.

entries.label: Monthly FPL table vs annual FPG ratio at the 200% limit
entries.description: 12 households are PE-eligible but Axiom-ineligible; 11 have household weight 0. All traced cases are near-threshold categorical-income cases where Axiom applies the FY 2026 SNAP monthly 100% FPL table times the encoded 2.00 multiplier while PE uses an annual FPG ratio. The one weighted case, ecps-39817, has Axiom gross income $7,256.55/month against a $7,192/month Axiom threshold while PE computes an annual FPG ratio of 1.963 and accepts. Resolving it requires an encoder/source decision about which FPG table controls NC's 200% limit.

entries.label: Joint-return self-employment deduction entity shape
entries.description: All 172 remaining federal mismatches (of 299,993 compared values) are EITC: 113 `eitc_earned_income` and 59 `eitc_reduction`, every one a joint return. Axiom's live RuleSpec still shapes 26 USC 1402(a), 1402(b), and 32(c)(2) around aggregate tax-unit self-employment inputs, while PE computes the SE-tax deduction per filer and sums non-dependent filers, which changes the OASDI wage-cap interaction. All other federal surfaces (CTC, standard deduction, tax before credits, capital gains, CDCC, AOTC, capped credits, OASDI/Medicare) match 100%.

drivers.label: Person-level SE tax chain collapsed to the tax unit
drivers.description: Every Axiom `eitc_earned_income` residual value matches an aggregate Section 1402(b)/164(f) model; the per-filer OASDI cap is what PE applies differently.
evidence: 45 of the 113 earned-income residual tax units have PE's Social Security SE taxable income capped below Medicare SE income for at least one filer.
Max absolute diff: $11,439.03 (eitc_earned_income), $2,409.04 (eitc_reduction).

drivers.label: Kept visible pending person-scoped re-encode
drivers.description: Replacing the encoded earned-income chain with PE's helper would hide the entity-shape boundary. Encoder guardrails block new unit-scope formulas composing the stale 1402(a) imports; the staged person-scoped re-encode of 1402(a)/(b), 164(f), and 32(c)(2) has not yet landed.
evidence: A no-manual 26 USC 1402(a) rerun deferred on unresolved exception branches; a narrower 1402(a)(12) rerun failed validation and was not applied.

entries.label: Six zero-weight tax-unit residuals
entries.description: Colorado runs end to end through the generated tax bridge with no missing inputs. All 6 remaining amount differences (of 926 tax units) are zero-weight ECPS rows, so the weighted match rate is 100% while the unweighted score is 920/926. Examples: ecps-tax-unit-131265 (+$154.46) and ecps-tax-unit-131530 (-$268.46). They need a component trace, not an output patch; no Python amount override is applied.

entries.label: Second-band base-amount rounding convention
entries.description: The 3 mismatches in this synthetic component check are the expected second-band convention difference: Axiom uses the rounded base amounts printed in the NYC IT-201 instructions ($37 joint, $25 head of household, $21 single/separate), while PolicyEngine derives unrounded carry-ins from the first-band rate and threshold ($36.936, $24.624, $20.52). Bracket shapes and rates agree; NYC CDCC components match 5/5.

entries.label: Second-band base-amount rounding convention
entries.description: All 81,197 school-tax rate-reduction mismatches in the full ECPS diagnostic are second-band cases of the same convention difference: Axiom uses the rounded IT-201 base amounts ($37/$25/$21 by filing status) while PE derives unrounded carry-ins ($36.936/$24.624/$20.52), giving per-case differences of $0.06 to $0.48. First-band, over-limit, and zero-or-negative cases all match (56,718/137,915), and the NYC CDCC slice matches 137,915/137,915. This diagnostic compares component formulas with PE upstream inputs, not final NYC liability.

entries.label: Outstanding-balance cap not yet encoded
entries.description: All 43 student-loan mismatches (of 115,710 compared people; the full run compares 3,451,998 values) are cases where PolicyEngine caps the repayment at the positive EFRS `student_loan_balance` while Axiom applies the GOV.UK plan/rate/threshold formula uncapped. Every residual has PE exactly equal to the balance (e.g. person_3512002: Axiom GBP 1,901.53 vs PE = balance GBP 294.12). The cap stays a visible mismatch until it is added through RuleSpec/encoder work; no projection override is applied.

entries.label: Reported-receipt rows below statutory age gate
entries.description: The 152 Carer's Allowance residuals are rows where PolicyEngine UK pays from reported Carer's Allowance receipt even though the EFRS person age is under 16. The refreshed Axiom GOV.UK wrapper enforces the source age-16 eligibility gate. The oracle projects positive PE/reported receipt to the statutory 35-hour care condition because current EFRS care_hours is zero on reported-receipt rows, but it does not override the age gate.

entries.label: Reported-receipt rows below statutory age gate
entries.description: The 12 Carer Support Payment residuals mirror the Carer's Allowance pattern: PolicyEngine UK pays from reported receipt on under-16 rows, while the source-backed Axiom wrapper keeps the statutory age-16 gate. The comparison leaves those rows visible rather than projecting age from the PE final award.

entries.label: PE pays higher mobility before age 3
entries.description: The 34 child DLA mobility residuals are children aged 0-2 where PolicyEngine UK has a higher-rate DLA mobility category and pays the weekly mobility component. The GOV.UK child DLA wrapper requires age 3 or over for higher-rate mobility and age 5 or over for lower-rate mobility, so Axiom returns zero for this component.

entries.label: Downstream of under-age mobility component
entries.description: The 34 child DLA annual-amount residuals are the annualized effect of the same age 0-2 higher-rate mobility rows. The care component agrees; the annual amount differs because PolicyEngine includes the mobility component while the source-backed Axiom child DLA wrapper applies the GOV.UK mobility age threshold.

entries.label: NBER TAXSIM child/dependent credit gaps
entries.description: All 4 federal liability mismatches in the PE-vs-TAXSIM check trace to documented TAXSIM modeling gaps, not adapter or projection bugs: TAXSIM does not model the $500 Other Dependent Credit, computes CTC at $1,700/child instead of the statutory $2,000, and omits the refundable ACTC when tax liability is zero. See docs/triage-pe-taxsim-residuals.md for the case-level decomposition.

entries.label: NBER TAXSIM child/dependent credit gaps
entries.description: The 3 CTC mismatches are the credit-level view of the same TAXSIM gaps driving the liability differences: no $500 ODC for adult dependents, $1,700/child instead of $2,000/child when liability can absorb the full non-refundable CTC, and no refundable ACTC at zero liability. PE applies the statutory amounts. See docs/triage-pe-taxsim-residuals.md.

entries.label: Legacy bridge taxable-income residuals
entries.description: This is the early federal oracle-bridge synthetic run, predating the full fiit-ecps pipeline. 4 of 813 tax units disagree on federal taxable income (diffs $1,534 to $21,106); the tax-before-credits and liability mismatches on the same tax units are downstream of this. The current full ECPS federal run compares taxable income and tax before credits cleanly, so the remaining work is to refresh or retire this legacy report rather than re-trace it.

entries.label: Downstream of legacy taxable-income residuals
entries.description: The 4 tax-before-credits mismatches are the same tax units as the taxable-income residuals (ecps-tax-unit-5012, 64926, 68364, 71824); the rate calculation amplifies the upstream taxable-income difference. The current full fiit-ecps run compares this surface cleanly.

entries.label: Downstream of legacy taxable-income residuals
entries.description: The 4 liability mismatches are the same tax units as the taxable-income residuals (ecps-tax-unit-5012, 64926, 68364, 71824) — liability differences track tax-before-credits almost exactly, so no separate credit-stage cause is indicated. The current full fiit-ecps run compares federal surfaces cleanly except the documented EITC entity-shape residuals.

entries.label: PolicyEngine 2026 taxable maximum is a Trustees projection
entries.description: PolicyEngine carries $186,000 for the 2026 OASDI contribution and benefit base, a Trustees-report projection. SSA's announced 2026 base, encoded from the Federal Register determination, is $184,500 ($60,600 x AWI-2024/AWI-1992, rounded to the nearest $300).

entries.label: PolicyEngine uprates 2025 value; SSA announced 2026 amount differs
entries.description: PolicyEngine has no transcribed 2026 value for this parameter and projects it by AWI uprating of the 2025 value (unrounded), while the rulespec encodes SSA's announced 2026 determination including the statutory rounding step. The Axiom values match SSA's published 2026 figures exactly.

entries.description: PolicyEngine has no transcribed 2026 value for this parameter and projects it by AWI uprating of the 2025 value (unrounded), while the rulespec encodes SSA's announced 2026 determination including the statutory rounding step. The Axiom values match SSA's published 2026 figures exactly.

The Axiom values match SSA's published 2026 figures exactly.

The Axiom values match SSA's published 2026 figures exactly.

The Axiom values match SSA's published 2026 figures exactly.

entries.label: GA parent/caretaker standard is dollar-based; PolicyEngine carries an FPL approximation
entries.description: Georgia's parent/caretaker Medicaid standard is published as dollar amounts (the encoding flags georgia_parent_caretaker_standard_uses_dollar_amounts), which the source approximates at 28% FPL + the 5% MAGI disregard (0.33). PolicyEngine carries 0.39 FPL from its 2018-vintage state table. Neither side is wrong per se — the comparison flags that PE's approximation predates the current published standard.

entries.label: PolicyEngine carries the SSI FBR as Colorado's OAP grant standard
entries.description: PolicyEngine's gov.states.co.ssa.state_supplement.grant_standard values ($943 in 2024, $967 in 2025) equal the federal SSI benefit rate for those years, but Colorado's Old Age Pension total grant standard is set by state rule above the FBR — 9 CCR 2503-5 sec. 3.530 sets $1,032 effective January 1, 2026. The parameter appears to conflate the OAP standard with the FBR and lacks a 2026 value.

entries.label: Statutory entitlement vs dataset SSI (take-up, imputed resources, deeming, couples)
entries.description: Of 3,231 divergences over 41,314 households (92.2% match), the dominant class remains the dataset withholding SSI from statutorily entitled people (take-up seeding, imputed-resource tests, spousal deeming — all dataset-side). Eligible couples are now paid at half the couple FBR each via a two-ABD-adults approximation; remaining couple noise and 1382c(f) ineligible-spouse deeming (not yet encoded upstream) account for most of the both-pay-differ residue. Dashboard copy shows the first 1,000 mismatches.

drivers.label: Take-up and imputed resources (dataset side)
drivers.description: The dataset withholds SSI from some entitled people (take-up seed false, or imputed resources above the $2,000/$3,000 limits). Axiom pays the statutory amount; the dataset pays zero.

drivers.label: Spousal deeming not yet encoded
drivers.description: 42 USC 1382c(f) income deeming from an ineligible spouse is outside the v1 composition, so Axiom pays aged/disabled people whose high-earning spouses disqualify them in the dataset.

drivers.label: Couple approximation edges
drivers.description: Couples are detected as 'two aged/blind/disabled adults in one household', so unmarried ABD pairs and 3+ ABD households diverge from PolicyEngine's marital-unit treatment.

entries.label: Earned income disregard rate and shelter schedule differ between the sources
entries.description: 58 of 2,288 NY households diverge, in two clean classes. 32 (Axiom pays more, all working households): the encoded 2024-2026 state plan applies a 62% earned income disregard while PolicyEngine carries 50%. 26 (PolicyEngine pays more, all no-earnings renters): the two sides carry different local-agency shelter maximum schedules (PE 277/283/400… vs the encoded 214/219/309… by household size), and the difference equals the per-size schedule gap exactly.

entries.label: MAGI income definition and the 435.603(d) 5% disregard
entries.description: 52 of 694 CO households have an adult PolicyEngine deems expansion-eligible where the composed 435.119 does not. Two drivers: PolicyEngine compares MAGI (taxable Social Security, tax-unit composition) while the projection uses gross cash income over the whole household; and PolicyEngine applies the 138% effective limit (133% + the 435.603(d) disregard) where the composed rule carries the statutory 133% — the disregard lives in 435.603, outside this composition.

entries.label: Household-unit and income-definition edges
entries.description: 4 cases where the composed rule finds an eligible adult and PolicyEngine does not — tax-unit household composition and MAGI additions on the PolicyEngine side.

entries.label: EUROMOD applies the February 2025 work-bonus table to January
entries.description: The 30k Belgium worker residual is the open JRC EUROMOD BE_2025 timing issue: EUROMOD appears to apply the February-through-December ONSS worker work-bonus table to all 12 months, while Axiom applies the separate January 2025 statutory table for one month and the February table for 11 months.

entries.label: Downstream of the EUROMOD work-bonus timing issue
entries.description: The net employee-contribution residual is exactly the opposite side of the worker work-bonus residual. The gross 13.07% employee contribution before reductions matches EUROMOD exactly; only the reduction timing differs.

entries.label: EUROMOD cumulates Wallonia Article 13 supplement on pre-2020 children
entries.description: The six older-child residuals are the open JRC EUROMOD BE_2025 transition issue: age-0 new-system Wallonia Article 13 cases match exactly, but pre-2020 children receive an extra annualized Article 13 supplement in EUROMOD. The middle-income residual is 31.09 * 12; the low-income residual is 68.39 * 12 on top of the statutory legacy LGAF low-income path. Walloon Articles 120, 123, and 128 keep pre-2020 LGAF amounts and bar cumulation with decree supplements.
